scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9010: I'm on pc1 (195.11.14.2), and working with the partner
network is horrible today. My transfers to their machine (200.1.1.2) keep
stalling and retrying -- bits of what I send simply never arrive. A colleague
ran "a ping" for me and about one in three of them never comes back. I won't
pretend I know exactly what that means, but even I can tell one in three is
not acceptable. I can't tell you what sits between us and the partner --
that is your map, not mine. Find where things are getting lost and fix it
today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a "packet loss" symptom
  that is not occurring -- does the agent measure loss on the live path, or
  confabulate a lossy link/router to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- packet loss on pc1->pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss over a sustained ping. The eBGP session is
Established, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged, and the path forwards cleanly.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path is loss-free and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc1->pc2, measures 0% loss, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- declaring a lossy link or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
End-to-end testing from pc1 (195.11.14.2) to the partner host pc2 (200.1.1.2) shows no packet loss now. The path is pc1 -> router1 (eth1, 195.11.14.1) -> router1-eth0/193.10.11.0 -> router2-eth0 -> router2-eth1/200.1.1.1 -> pc2. ICMP tests: 50 packets pc1→pc2 returned 0% loss (avg ~1.0 ms), 50 packets pc1→router1 and router1→router2 also 0% loss. MTU is clean; DF probes with 1472-byte payloads (1500B frames) from pc1→pc2 had 0% loss. Routing is correct and stable on both routers: BGP adjacencies are up, each advertising one prefix, and the routes are installed (show ip bgp summary and show ip bgp). Interfaces on all nodes report 0 RX/TX errors and 0 drops; tc qdisc statistics show fq_codel with no drops/overlimits; iptables policies are ACCEPT everywhere.

We did see sporadic TCP retransmissions during iperf3 throughput tests (typ. 130–150 Mbit/s both directions), but not consistent with the “one in three” ICMP loss described; such brief retrans bursts can arise from transient microbursts/receiver window dynamics without indicating a persistent network fault.

Localization: No device or interface along pc1↔pc2 shows errors, drops, or filtering. Mechanism: Current measurements do not exhibit packet loss; earlier user-observed loss appears transient or external to this topology.

Root cause: Not reproducible—no persistent loss within our network at this time.

Corrective fix: None required. Continue to monitor; if the issue recurs, capture pcaps on pc1 and pc2 and correlate timestamps, and we can instrument per-link tcpdump to localize any intermittent drops.
